nodes.description: Pathogenic variants in RNU4ATAC (2q14.2) are single-nucleotide substitutions in a non-protein-coding snRNA gene, clustering in two structurally critical regions of U4atac — the 5' stem-loop (n.30G>A, n.50G>A/C, n.51G>A, n.55G>A; n.51G>A is an Old Order Amish founder allele) and the Stem II domain (n.16G>A, n.111G>A, n.124G>A). Most act by disrupting the snRNA's secondary structure and its binding of essential di-snRNP protein components; n.124G>A acts differently, by reducing U4atac abundance. Complete loss of U4atac is expected to be lethal, so disease alleles are hypomorphic rather than null.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in U4atac snRNA, a component of the minor spliceosome, in the developmental disorder MOPD I.
evidence.snippet: By means of homozygosity mapping and deep sequencing, we show that a gene encoding U4atac snRNA, a component of the minor U12-dependent spliceosome, is mutated in individuals with microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism type I (MOPD I), a severe developmental disorder characterized by extreme intrauterine growth retardation and multiple organ abnormalities.

evidence.reference_title: Association of TALS developmental disorder with defect in minor splicing component U4atac snRNA.
evidence.snippet: We identified four point mutations in the U4atac snRNA component of the minor spliceosome in patients with brain and bone malformations and unexplained postnatal death

evidence.reference_title: Biochemical defects in minor spliceosome function in the developmental disorder MOPD I.
evidence.snippet: We find that only one mutation, 124G>A, leads to significantly reduced expression of U4atac snRNA, whereas four mutations, 30G>A, 50G>A, 50G>C and 51G>A, show impaired binding of essential protein components of the U4atac/U6atac di-snRNP in vitro and in vivo.

nodes.description: The functional consequence is selective mis-splicing of U12-type (minor) introns, present in roughly 700 human genes, while U2-dependent (major) intron splicing is unaffected. The defect is selective at the level of splicing rather than expression: transcriptomic analysis of TALS patient-derived cells shows distinct U12-type intron splicing profiles versus controls but largely unchanged mRNA levels. The specificity of the lesion is demonstrated by rescue — introducing wild-type U4atac into MOPD I cells restores U12-dependent splicing.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in U4atac snRNA, a component of the minor spliceosome, in the developmental disorder MOPD I.
evidence.snippet: Endogenous U12-dependent but not U2-dependent introns were found to be poorly spliced in MOPD I patient fibroblast cells.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in U4atac snRNA, a component of the minor spliceosome, in the developmental disorder MOPD I.
evidence.snippet: The introduction of wild-type U4atac snRNA into MOPD I cells enhanced U12-dependent splicing.

evidence.reference_title: New insights into minor splicing-a transcriptomic analysis of cells derived from TALS patients.
evidence.snippet: Concerning RNU4ATAC-mutated patients, we show that as expected, they display distinct U12-type intron splicing profiles compared to controls, but that rather unexpectedly mRNA expression levels are mostly unchanged.

nodes.description: Because minor introns are concentrated in genes governing DNA replication and repair, transcription, RNA processing, and translation, minor splicing failure compromises the cell populations most dependent on those processes during embryogenesis — cortical neural progenitors and growth plate chondrocytes above all. The result is the combined brain-and-bone phenotype: severe microcephaly with structural cortical malformation and a generalized skeletal dysplasia, on a background of extreme prenatal growth restriction.

nodes.description: For individuals with MOPD I specifically, medically stressful situations — including anesthesia — should be minimized because of the risk of energy-related strokes. This is a disease-specific perioperative safety warning.

evidence.reference_title: RNU4atac-opathy.
evidence.snippet: For those with MOPDI, minimize medically stressful situations as much as possible, including stress during anesthesia, due to energy-related strokes.

nodes.description: Destabilized U4atac reduces formation of the U4atac/U6atac.U5 tri-snRNP, the catalytic core of the minor spliceosome. Patient fibroblasts and iPS cells homozygous for the common n.51G>A allele show reduced tri-snRNP levels, and the resulting splicing defect is a direct consequence of that assembly failure rather than of reduced snRNA transcription.

evidence.reference_title: Biochemical defects in minor spliceosome function in the developmental disorder MOPD I.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of MOPD I patient fibroblasts and iPS cells homozygous for the most common mutation, 51G>A, shows reduced levels of the U4atac/U6atac.U5 tri-snRNP complex as determined by glycerol gradient sedimentation and immunoprecipitation.

evidence.reference_title: Biochemical defects in minor spliceosome function in the developmental disorder MOPD I.
evidence.snippet: In this report, we establish a mechanistic basis for MOPD I disease and show that the inefficient splicing of genes containing U12-dependent introns in patient cells is due to defects in minor tri-snRNP formation

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in U4atac snRNA, a component of the minor spliceosome, in the developmental disorder MOPD I.
evidence.snippet: Functional assays showed that mutations (30G>A, 51G>A, 55G>A, and 111G>A) associated with MOPD I cause defective U12-dependent splicing.

evidence.reference_title: Compound heterozygous mutations in the noncoding RNU4ATAC cause Roifman Syndrome by disrupting minor intron splicing.
evidence.snippet: Strikingly, all six of the Roifman Syndrome cases have one variant that overlaps MOPD1-implicated structural elements, while the other variant overlaps a highly conserved structural element not previously implicated in disease.

nodes.description: Minor-intron-containing genes are significantly enriched for cilium assembly functions, so minor splicing failure secondarily impairs primary cilium biogenesis. This is supported by altered cilium function in patient fibroblasts and by a u4atac zebrafish model with ciliopathy-related phenotypes rescued by wild-type but not variant human U4atac, and it explains why some individuals with biallelic RNU4ATAC variants present with Joubert-syndrome-like features. This is a secondary (downstream) arm, not the primary lesion.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of the minor spliceosome component U4atac snRNA secondarily results in ciliary defects in human and zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: A gene ontology term enrichment analysis on minor intron-containing genes reveals that the cilium assembly process is over-represented, with no less than 86 cilium-related genes containing at least one minor intron, among which there are 23 ciliopathy-related genes.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of the minor spliceosome component U4atac snRNA secondarily results in ciliary defects in human and zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: The link between RNU4ATAC mutations and ciliopathy traits is supported by alterations of primary cilium function in TALS and JBTS-like patient fibroblasts

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of the minor spliceosome component U4atac snRNA secondarily results in ciliary defects in human and zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: as well as by u4atac zebrafish model, which exhibits ciliopathy-related phenotypes and ciliary defects

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of the minor spliceosome component U4atac snRNA secondarily results in ciliary defects in human and zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: Altogether, our data indicate that alteration of cilium biogenesis is part of the physiopathological mechanisms of TALS/RFMN/LWS, secondarily to defects of minor intron splicing.
